Adam, ſlaues of the diuel, not only ſubiect to temporal death, but alſo
are excluded for euer from heauenly bliſe and glorie: except by Chriſts redem-
ption particularly applied, they be reſtored to grace & iuſtice in this life.
And touching Adam and Eue, whoſe ſinne was not original but actual,
directly committed by them ſelues, Gods mercie ſo reclamed them by new
grace, that they deſpared not (as Cain, and ſome orhers did afterwards) but
with hope of remiſſion Were ſorie and penitent, and accord:ngly receiued
penance, and redemption. For God brought Adam from his ſinne (as sap, t0.
holie writte teſtifieth) and the ſame is collected of Eue, God shewing the
like ſignes of bis prouident mercie towyards them both, of which we shal by
and by note ſome for example.
Now let vs ſee the more principal points of faith and Religion profeſſed
and ohſerued by the Church of God before Woes floud. Firſt they beleeued in
one Eternal and Omnipotent God, who made the whole world and al thi ngs
therin of nothing. which is eaſely confeſſed of al that are not plaine Atheiſto,
and may be proued againſt them by reaſon. Aad therfore Adam and
other Patriarches could not erre in this Article, nor others be ignorant theroſ,
except they were very wicked.
The Myſterie alſo of the Bleſſed Trinitie, three Diui ne Perſons in one God,
though farre aboue the reach of mans reaſon, yet Was beleued more expreſly
by ſome, more implied by others, and conſerued from age to age by tradition,
at leaſt amongſt the chiefe heades and leaders. wherupon Moyſes afterwardes
inſinuated the ſame great alyſterie, by diuers wordes and phraſes, writing
God and his workes. The two wordes God created if they be richtly con-
ſidered importe ſo mach. For the word Elohim, God, in the plural number,
ſignifyeth pluralitie of Perſons (for manie Gods it can not ſigniſte, ſeeing
there is but one God) and the verbe bara, created, in the ſingular number
ſignifyeth one God in nature and ſubſtance, albeit three Perſons. For what-
ſoeuer God doth in creatures, is the wor be of the whole Trinitre : though helie
worke ioynt- Screpeures do oftentimes appropriate ſome worke to one Diuine Perſon, ſome
ly in al crea- to an other. which alſo proueth diſtinction of Perſons in God. So the wordes
